current_episode.title: How To Triple The Size Of An Accounting Firm With Authentic Leadership - Winning with Krista Rabidoux, Managing Director at Andersen

guest.bio_context: Krista came from an arts background and started her career in concert production and stage management before being encouraged by professor Grant McEwen at Grant MacEwan University to pursue accounting. She later developed expertise as a coach and family enterprise advisor. She joined Anderson seven years ago as Managing Director to rebuild and transform the boutique accounting firm from an owner-managed business into a scaled organization.

pending_qa.q: How does Krista distinguish her advisory approach from the Big Four accounting firm model?
pending_qa.r: At Big Four firms, Krista worked in a rigid environment focused on getting returns and ensuring compliance. At Anderson's boutique model, she brings her authentic self and can provide holistic, customized advice by combining her accounting expertise with creative problem-solving from her arts background, allowing her to view client situations from multiple angles.

pending_qa.q: What is Krista's philosophy on authentic leadership and employee engagement?
pending_qa.r: Krista believes that people can achieve success externally but will never feel successful until they show up authentically. She tells her team that receiving success and feeling successful are different—the latter requires being true to oneself. This creates inherent trust because when people are authentic, the energy flows properly rather than causing observers to question truthfulness.

pending_qa.q: How does Krista address self-doubt and mental health in her leadership journey?
pending_qa.r: Krista acknowledges that all entrepreneurs experience self-doubt and limiting beliefs about whether they're doing the right thing or will succeed. She emphasizes work-life integration rather than balance and focuses on programming her brain through affirmations like 'everything's OK and it's going to be OK,' recognizing that the brain is highly programmable and success starts internally.

pending_qa.q: What did Krista learn from her arts background that applies to her professional leadership?
pending_qa.r: From her stage management experience, Krista learned that the show must go on regardless of what happens backstage or what goes wrong. This mindset translates to professional resilience: when things go sideways, the business continues and performance depends on how you show up despite challenges, not on whether external circumstances are perfect.

pending_qa.q: Why does Krista reject the stereotypical accountant identity and how does this differentiate Anderson?
